_README: CALLS THAT ARE ON A CLIENT'S TRACKER BUT ARE NOT THAT CLIENT'S BUSINESS.
A closer who sells more than one offer books all of it into one tracker,
because the tracker belongs to the closer's calendar, not to the offer. So a
sale can be recorded correctly and still not be ours to count. Nothing in the
data says which offer a call was for — Brey's tracker has no Offer field, and
the closer, the price and the outcome all look identical either way.
WHY A LIST AND NOT A RULE. There is no signal that separates these safely.
The obvious candidate — money recorded as taken on the call that never
appears in the client's payment processor — was tested against Brey's live
account on 2026-08-22 and matched exactly two calls, one of which (Liam) was
an ordinary Funded Blueprint sale whose 'collected on call' figure had simply
been typed wrong. A rule like that would quietly delete a real sale every
time a payment failed to match. So exclusions are named by a person, one at a
time, with the reason attached.
THE COST OF THIS FILE, STATED PLAINLY: it only holds calls somebody thought
to add. As the other offer sells more, this list goes stale and the client's
revenue reads high, with nothing on any screen saying so. The durable fix is
an Offer field on the tracker that the closer sets. Until that exists, every
command that reads this file also prints how many calls it excluded, and the
Sales Command Center says on the page how many rows it left out, so the list
cannot rot silently.
MATCHED ON recording_share_id FIRST, then notion_page_id, then call_date +
prospect_name. Prefer the recording: it identifies the CALL, and survives the
row being deleted and re-created by the automation. A page id identifies one
ROW and dies with it. The name is the weakest of the three — the row below is
named literally 'Unknown', and two Unknown rows on one date would be
indistinguishable, so excluding one would exclude both.
a notion_page_id.
BEFORE YOU ADD A ROW, ASK WHOP WHETHER THE MONEY ARRIVED. A tracker row with
no prospect email reads as unmatched whoever paid, so 'the processor never saw
this cash' is a statement about the missing email, not about whose sale it is.
One row was excluded on that reasoning on 2026-08-22 and put back on 2026-08-24
once the payment was found. Search the payments by the buyer's own name.
AN EXCLUDED CALL IS NEVER TURNED INTO A LEAD, so it cannot reach revenue, the
close rate or the funnel even if somebody later types an email onto the row.
TWO COPIES, ONE FILE. The Sales Command Center and the KPI dashboard deploy
independently and cannot read each other, so each repository carries its own
copy. Copy this file WHOLE; never edit one side. Both repos run
`npm run check:rules`, which compares the copies when they sit side by side.

(3) No payment from Ludgero Teixeira has ever entered Brey's Whop account, checked across all 475 payments on 2026-08-24, unlike Jonathan Laguna whose money is there.

Tpan's own sheet dates Antonio 8/22 and gives his row Jonathan's recording link, which is what made three separate people look like two. Antonio Cepeda has no call in Tpan's Fathom and no row on the tracker at all.

Funded Blueprint.row_archived_in_notion: 2026-08-24. The row itself was removed from Brey's tracker, so this entry is now a backstop: it holds if the row is ever restored from Notion's trash, or if the same call is recorded again.
Funded Blueprint.why_the_recording_id_is_the_key: The Notion row was archived on 2026-08-24, and the automation is being widened to accept impromptu recordings — which would re-import this exact call as a NEW row with a new page id, silently escaping a page-id-only entry. The Fathom share id identifies the call itself and survives that.

Funded Blueprint.reason: Sold on JP EMBRACE, a third offer running through the same recorder - not Funded Blueprint. Four independent sources agree and none of them is the tracker: (1) Tpan's Fathom summary states the purpose outright, 'Qualify Carmine for the JP Embrace mentorship and close the sale'; (2) Tpan's own sheet marks the row DQ / cancelled, not won; (3) Brey's Whop holds no payment from Carmine at all, checked across all 131 payments on 2026-08-25; (4) the tracker itself is the only thing claiming a $2,000 Customer, and it got there because the scorer read a close in the transcript - which there was, on somebody else's offer.
Funded Blueprint.ruled_by: Claude, 2026-08-25, on Moayad's instruction to do whatever is most accurate
Funded Blueprint.what_it_corrects: Carmine was one of the five 'closes the closer says never closed' found in the 17-23 August audit. This is the first of the five with a positive explanation rather than an absence: the money was never missing, the sale was never Brey's. Removes $2,000 of revenue and one close from August that no payment ever backed.
Funded Blueprint.not_the_same_as: Ignacio Valera, 2026-08-08, also a JP Embrace call by the summary - deliberately NOT excluded. He paid Brey's own Whop $25 on the day, so unlike Carmine there is a real relationship on this account. $25 is under the $100 deposit floor, so he was never counted as a close and removing him would delete a real customer to fix a number that was never wrong.
Funded Blueprint.also_blocked_at_the_gate: The workflow now refuses a call whose Fathom purpose names JP Embrace, FBA or Amazon, so a fourth one cannot arrive the same way. This entry is the backstop for the row already written.

Funded Blueprint.why_it_matters: Scored as a sales call it would count as a call held that closed nobody, so it lowers the close rate while telling you nothing. One row is trivial; the shape is not, since every future team huddle started outside the booking link looks identical to the gate.
